findings.description: `forceApprove(nftMinter, type(uint256).max)` is granted for the whole mint loop instead of the caller's actual budget. Because the minter pulls from the BATCHER's balance (not from a per-caller ledger), an under-funded batch does not revert as documented — the shortfall is silently covered by whatever payment-token balance the contract already holds (third-party donations, dispatcher-side dust accumulated below DUST_THRESHOLD across prior batches). Directly contradicts the contract NatSpec at src/BatchNFTMinter.sol:69-71 ('If `paymentAmount` falls short of the dispatcher's cumulative charge an inner `mint` reverts and the entire batch atomically rolls back') and §3 step 5/6 of docs/multi-token-nudge.md.
findings.attackVector: Caller passes paymentAmount = cumulativeCost - X where X <= the contract's own payment-token balance. The loop completes; the caller receives `count` NFTs for less than `count` mints' worth of payment; `totalPaid` under-reports the true dispatcher cost. Distinct route to the same pot as LOCAL-BM20-002 (step-10 sweep) — critically, the profile's recommended fix for BM20-002 (bound the sweep to the caller's unspent budget) does NOT close this route, so the two must be fixed together.
findings.secondaryImpact: Cross-repo trust coupling. The max allowance is contained ONLY by NFTMinterV2's property that `_executeMint` pulls from `msg.sender` (lib/mutable/yield-claim-nft/src/NFTMinterV2.sol:183). That invariant lives in a different repo, is not asserted here, and is exactly what an attacker-controlled `onERC1155Received` running mid-loop would need to break to drain the batcher. PoC test 1 confirms the allowance is observably `type(uint256).max` inside attacker code and that today it CANNOT be tapped.
findings.recommendation: Approve `paymentAmount` rather than `type(uint256).max`. Functionally identical (paymentAmount is by construction the entire budget the loop may spend), restores the documented fail-closed behaviour on under-funding, and removes the cross-repo dependence on 'the minter only ever pulls from msg.sender'.
findings.lawRef: Law 2 (documented behaviour is false) + Law 1 defense-in-depth

findings.severityNote: Escalates to Medium if a dispatcher whose primeToken() equals an accumulated reward asset is ever registered at the pinned index.
findings.description: The §4.1 exclusion key and the payment asset are both derived live from `dispatcher.primeToken()`. Changing the dispatcher — either by `NFTMinterV2.replaceDispatcher(index, ...)` in the SIBLING repo, or by `setDispatcherIndex` here — silently reclassifies the contract's existing balances. If the new dispatcher's primeToken is an asset the contract has been accumulating as a nudge pot (mainnet today: BalancerPoolerV2 primeToken = USDS, donation = USDC delivered to batchMinter at BalancerPoolerV2.sol:260), the accumulated USDC pot instantly (a) becomes un-listable as a reward — every caller listing it reverts BatchMint__RewardTokenIsPaymentToken — and (b) becomes fully sweepable by ANY `count = 1` caller via the step-10 dust sweep (line 381-387), with no nudgeSize gate.
findings.attackVector: Operator repoints the dispatcher (a routine migration action in a different repo with no on-chain coupling to BatchNFTMinter). The next single-mint transaction sweeps the entire accumulated pot for the price of one mint. This re-creates precisely the honeypot condition that §1 of docs/multi-token-nudge.md declares impossible ('there is no configuration of this mechanism under which claiming is profitable-in-isolation') — a pot accumulated over N batches can exceed one mint's price by orders of magnitude.
findings.ownerTrustAnalysis: Law 3: this is NOT a malicious-owner vector. A competent, non-malicious operator performing a dispatcher migration would be surprised that it drains the nudge pot to an arbitrary MEV bot at 1/nudgeSize the intended cost, because the coupling is invisible from the yield-claim-nft side. Surprise ⇒ footgun ⇒ in scope.
findings.recommendation: Operational: add 'pause BatchNFTMinter and rescueERC20 the pot' as a mandatory pre-step in any dispatcher-repoint runbook. Code: bound the step-10 sweep to the caller's own unspent budget (`paymentAmount - amountSpent`) rather than `balanceOf(address(this))` — this closes the leak for any asset, present or future, and is the same fix LOCAL-BM20-002 needs.
findings.lawRef: Law 3 (non-obvious footgun) + Law 2 (§1 honeypot argument broken)

findings.description: The inbound ERC1155 acceptance hook `onERC1155Received(recipient)` fires once per mint INSIDE the loop (real path: NFTMinterV2.sol:196 -> OZ ERC1155._mint -> _doSafeTransferAcceptanceCheck), i.e. `count` executions of attacker-chosen code between the pre-loop reward snapshot (line 354) and the post-loop payout (line 378), while the contract holds the caller's whole payment budget and a live max allowance. NO TEST IN THE SUITE EXERCISES THIS SURFACE: the mock minter mints via `MockERC1155.mint()` (test/mocks/MockERC1155.sol:28-32), a bare balance write that skips `_checkOnERC1155Received` entirely. The only reentrancy witness, test_RevertWhen_RewardTokenReentersBatchMint (test/BatchNFTMinterMultiTokenNudge.t.sol:338-354), proves the guard ONLY at the reward-token `transfer` site, and only with an EMPTY nested reward array.
findings.verdict: The guard IS sufficient today — proven, not assumed. PoC test 1 wires a hook-firing minter mirroring the OZ acceptance check and confirms: the hook runs NUDGE_SIZE times mid-loop; it observes allowance == type(uint256).max and the full unpaid pot still on the contract; re-entry into batchMint reverts with the exact ReentrancyGuard.ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall selector; and a hook-driven `minter.mint()` pulls from the hook, not from the batcher (batcher payment balance unchanged across the probe).
findings.residualRisk: The property is unpinned. Any future change that (a) drops nonReentrant, (b) moves the reward snapshot or payout inside/after the loop, or (c) makes the batcher hold cross-call state, re-opens an attacker-controlled callback surface that no test would catch. §4.3 of the spec is currently certified by a witness that does not reach the hook it was written for.
findings.recommendation: Port PoC_BatchMinterCallbackAndAllowance.t.sol's HookingMinter/EvilRecipient into the project suite as the §4.3 receive-hook witness, alongside the existing transfer-site witness. Cheaper alternative: have MockITokenMinterV2 route through MockERC1155.safeTransferFrom (which does fire the hook) instead of the bare mint helper.
findings.lawRef: Law 1 (recall: an unexercised attacker-controlled callback is a live recall risk, not a cleared row)

findings.description: REFUTED as a value issue. `ITokenMinterV2.mint` declares `returns (bool success)`, but NFTMinterV2._executeMint (lib/mutable/yield-claim-nft/src/NFTMinterV2.sol:170-201) either reverts on its four require()s or returns an unconditional `true` at line 200 — there is no path that returns `false`. A caller can therefore NEVER be charged for `count` mints and receive fewer on the production path. Additionally, even against a hypothetical false-returning minter the caller is not over-charged: unspent budget is returned by the step-10 sweep and `totalPaid` floors at 0.
findings.residualRisk: A silent-no-op minter WOULD clear the `count >= nudgeSize` gate at zero real mint cost and pay out the full pot — the historical H-01 drain class. This is reachable only via an owner-set broken `tokenMinter`, which is an obvious misconfiguration (Law 3: trusted, suppress as a finding) — but the interface declares a success flag the contract chooses to discard.
findings.recommendation: `require(nftMinter.mint(_dispatcherIndex, recipient), "mint failed")`. Free, and it converts a cross-repo behavioural assumption into an on-chain assertion.
findings.verdict: no under-delivery possible; file as QA hardening only

findings.description: REFUTED. Modifier order is `whenNotPaused nonReentrant`, so `whenNotPaused` executes before the guard is armed. `Pausable.whenNotPaused` expands to `_requireNotPaused()` — a single SLOAD of `_paused` and a conditional revert. It makes NO external call and enters no user-controlled code, so there is no window in which foreign code runs before `_status` is set. Aderyn's rule is a stylistic convention here, not a live vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Reorder to `nonReentrant whenNotPaused` for convention-conformance only (zero behavioural change). Note for the InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator scanner: SAST-104/105 are the same rule at src/InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.sol:152 and :186 and require the same 'does the preceding modifier make an external call?' check independently — do not close them by reference to this entry.

findings.description: CORRECTION to the Tier-1 profile. The profile states the snapshot-pass `balanceOf` is 'view-typed but the callee is arbitrary and may mutate state — Solidity's `view` on `_snapshotRewards` constrains *this* contract, not the callee'. That is wrong: `IERC20.balanceOf` is itself declared `view`, so solc emits a STATICCALL at the call site regardless of the callee's implementation. A hostile reward token CANNOT mutate state, emit events, or mount a mutative re-entry from the snapshot pass — it can only revert (self-harm) or gas-bomb (self-paid). Proven by test_SnapshotBalanceOfIsStaticcall (a non-view `balanceOf` that writes storage bricks the batch; the control at count < nudgeSize, where the call site is skipped, succeeds).
findings.impact: Reduces the untrusted-reward-token attack surface from two arbitrary-code hooks to ONE (the `safeTransfer` at line 458). Combined with nonReentrant and the fact that the batcher grants no allowance on reward tokens to anybody, every hostile-token vector enumerated (revert-griefing, gas-bomb, inconsistent balanceOf between snapshot and payout, non-standard returns) is self-inflicted by the caller who supplied the array; no third party and no protocol invariant is reachable. Non-standard return values are handled by SafeERC20; a live balance below the snapshot reverts the batch; a token that delivers less than it reports is LOCAL-BM20-003 (FoT), already filed.

findings.description: The positional destructure `(address dispatcher,,,) = INFTMinterV2(...).configs(idx)` was deferred to interaction analysis against the phStaging YS-20 minter-repoint ABI-drift precedent (filed Medium there). ASSESSMENT: the YS-20 class does NOT apply at YS-20 severity here, for two independent reasons. (1) The exclusion key cannot silently desynchronize from the actual payment asset: BatchNFTMinter reads `dispatcher.primeToken()` (line 322) and NFTMinterV2._executeMint reads `ITokenDispatcherV2(config.dispatcher).primeToken()` (NFTMinterV2.sol:177) from the SAME dispatcher resolved from the SAME tuple position — a wrong-but-live dispatcher yields a wrong-but-CONSISTENT payment token and exclusion key, so §4.1 stays enforced against whatever the minter actually pulls. (2) A tuple REORDER that displaces `dispatcher` from position 0 fails closed: the decoded price-as-address has no code and `primeToken()` reverts on solc's extcodesize check, bricking batchMint rather than repointing it. An APPENDED field is tolerated (position 0 unchanged), which is the realistic forward-compatible drift.
findings.residualRisk: Fail-closed is a DoS, not a safe state, and it is emergent rather than asserted. There is no `dispatcherToIndex(dispatcher) == _dispatcherIndex` cross-check (the getter exists on INFTMinterV2) that would turn a silent-decode into an explicit error.
findings.recommendation: QA: add `require(INFTMinterV2(nftMinter).dispatcherToIndex(dispatcher) == _dispatcherIndex)` after line 321 as a cheap positional-drift tripwire. The genuinely material drift risk is the SEMANTIC one (dispatcher legitimately repointed to a different prime asset) — filed separately as CODE-BM20-102.
findings.verdict: not the YS-20 severity class; QA hardening

reentrancyChecklist.why: batchMint writes NO persistent state; the only cross-call effect is a transient allowance revoked at line 368 and rolled back atomically on any revert.

Both inbound hooks (ERC1155 receive at line 364, reward-token transfer at line 458) re-enter batchMint and hit ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall. Proven at BOTH sites — the transfer site by the project suite, the receive-hook site only by CODE-BM20-103's PoC.
Every other entry point is onlyOwner or onlyPauser. rescueERC20 is unguarded but owner-only and there is no persistent balance-derived state a re-entry could desynchronize.

reentrancyChecklist.status: cleared for this contract; ONE handoff
reentrancyChecklist.why: BatchNFTMinter exposes no balance-derived or price-derived view — its only public getters are tokenMinter/dispatcherIndex/nudgeSize/pauser, none of which move during batchMint. No integrator can be fed a torn read from this contract. HANDOFF: mid-loop, NFTMinterV2's configs[idx].price and ERC1155 totalSupply(id) advance count times, and the attacker-controlled receive-hook can call NFTStaker._recomputeSchedule (via stake/pullAndRefresh) at any chosen intermediate price. Each observation is a settled post-mint value (price is bumped at NFTMinterV2.sol:188 BEFORE _mint at :196), so this is NOT a torn read — but the attacker chooses WHICH of the count prices the staking schedule is sized against, repeatedly, in one tx. That is an emission/APY-sizing question, not a code-integrity one. ROUTED TO econ-scanner; explicitly NOT dropped.
No ERC721 anywhere in this contract's call graph.
See CODE-BM20-103 — surface is real and attacker-controlled, guard holds, but is untested.

paymentToken is USDS (no hooks, and the profile's semi-trusted assumption is the governing one). Reward tokens are arbitrary caller input, but per CODE-BM20-106 the only mutative site is the payout safeTransfer, which is guarded and reaches no third-party value.

edgeCasesVerified.verdict: clean — checked at line 304 before ANY external call, so a mismatched call cannot even probe the minter. _payRewards iterates snapshot.length and indexes rewardTokens[i]; the equality check is what makes that safe and it is unconditional.
clean — zero-length snapshot, zero-iteration passes, no reward, no event; legal per §2 and reachable independently of nudgeSize.
clean — available pinned to 0, floor check reverts. Intended per §3 step 4.

clean — amount == 0 continue, no transfer, no event. SAST-003 (dangerous strict equality on `amount == 0`) is a false positive: this is a sentinel test on an unsigned balance, not a rounding-sensitive comparison.
